title: LUA-12 (service call), LUA-15 (structured failure), LUA-16 (runtime error capture) need production code + tests
related_to: GH #495 / ISS-0169 -- parent (the LUA-08..16 verification tranche)
ISS-0161 -- Real LuaJIT bindings (the FFI surface LUA-15/16 actually depends on)
ISS-0153 -- Stub-era holdovers this run's tranche still has to clear
ISS-0172 / GH #500 -- test-root pin pattern (relevant to where new tests must live)
scope: src/lua/{call_service,fail,executor,events,service_catalog,host_context,instruction_limiter,memory_limiter}.zig and tests under src/lua/. No public-API change to executor.executeScript signature (LUA-04's tests and other callers depend on it), but ScriptResult gains a discriminator so LUA-15/LUA-16 can be distinguished.
symptom: ISS-0169 tranche 1 (PR #505) closed compilation across the LUA subsystem and made capability enforcement real, but did NOT deliver runtime behavior for three MUST requirements that tranche 1 explicitly deferred to later tranches: LUA-12 (call_service only simulates; ServiceCatalog.lookup() has zero callers), LUA-15 (platform.fail writes three script-reachable globals that nothing reads back, so an explicit failure is indistinguishable from any other runtime error), and LUA-16 (no captureStackTrace implementation; events.zig's ScriptErrorPayload / EventRecord are correctly typed but have zero construction sites -- pure dead types). See GH #592 for the upstream framing.
root_cause_analysis:
Three independent root causes, one per requirement, with a cross-cutting dependency between LUA-15 and LUA-16:

  (1) LUA-12 -- Deferral. ISS-0169 noted in src/lua/host_api/call_service.zig that 'after the gate passes it keeps its simulation path and its hardcoded {} non-simulation branch, does not consult service_catalog.zig'. The deferral scope was deliberate (LUA-12 was carved into its own tranche at scoping), but the design §17.1 already shows the intended implementation: ExecutionContext gains a *const ServiceCatalog field, platformCallService calls ctx.service_catalog.lookup(svc_id) to validate the service id before any HTTP path, the non-simulation path becomes a real HTTP call against the registered endpoint_url (or the design's table-returning shape, depending on the return-shape decision). The work was not done -- not lost, not partially-done.

  (2) LUA-15 -- Anti-forgery pattern not applied. host_context.zig already established the canonical 'put it in LUA_REGISTRYINDEX, not _G, not upvalues' channel for the ExecutionContext pointer (LUA-05/06). fail.zig was written before that pattern existed and was never migrated: __failure_reason__, __failure_details__, __explicit_failure__ are ordinary _G globals, script-writable, never read back. The fix is mechanical: register private keys (bpm.failure_reason / bpm.failure_details / bpm.explicit_failure) following the host_context.zig pattern, write there from platformFail, read back from executeSource's failed-pcall branch to decide between ExplicitFailure and RuntimeError in ScriptResult.

  (3) LUA-16 -- Dependency on LUA-08 + LUA-15. design §21.2 specifies a captureStackTrace using lua_getstack/lua_getinfo, and design §21.3 requires the ScriptErrorPayload to carry instruction_count (LUA-08) and memory_peak_bytes (LUA-09). Both LUA-08 and LUA-09 are themselves IN_PROGRESS (per docs/status/requirement_status.yaml) with the limiter files compiling but no call site wiring (installHook has zero callers in the source tree). LUA-16's captureStackTrace is independent (just needs lua_getstack/lua_getinfo walk), but the ScriptErrorPayload construction is blocked until LUA-08 and LUA-09 land in the same run -- otherwise instruction_count has no source and the field would always be 0 (a worse test outcome than missing).

  Cross-cutting: The executeSource pcall-failed branch in executor.zig currently records a single error_message and returns success=false regardless of whether the failure was an explicit platform.fail() or a true Lua runtime error (lines ~315-322 of executor.zig). Distinguishing the two requires the LUA-15 registry read to happen there. ScriptResult must gain a discriminator (e.g. an error_kind field with values .RuntimeError / .ExplicitFailure / .CompileError) so the engine (not the executor -- the executor still does no I/O per the transition.zig precedent) can emit the right SCRIPT_ERROR vs SCRIPT_FAILED event later.

  Severity: MAJOR. All three requirements are MUST and currently IN_PROGRESS with no path to RELEASED; the GH-495 parent scope (9 requirements) has now been split into 3 batches of which 2 (batch 1, the LUA-05/06 capability enforcement + LUA-07 manifest) are already in production; batches 2 (LUA-11/13, ISS-0624/GH-591) and 3 (this issue, LUA-12/15/16) remain.
impact: Without LUA-15: any platform.fail(reason) from a script is silently treated as a generic runtime error by the engine. Tests/specs/LUA-15.md TC-LUA-15-04 (SCRIPT_FAILED event emitted), TC-LUA-15-07 (explicit failure distinct from runtime error), TC-LUA-15-13 (instance routing on SCRIPT_FAILED) all FAIL because there is no SCRIPT_FAILED event path. Without LUA-16: uncaught Lua errors are recorded as bare error_message strings -- no stack trace, no instruction count, no capability-at-failure snapshot. Tests/specs/LUA-16.md TC-LUA-16-04 through -08 all FAIL. Without LUA-12: platform.call_service works in simulation only; the non-simulation branch returns a hardcoded '{}' regardless of svc_id, and even the simulation branch does not validate svc_id against the catalog (so the same fingerprint will hit a mock for a non-existent service). Tests/specs/LUA-12.md TC-LUA-12-04 (service not found returns error table) and TC-LUA-12-15 (network error returns structured error) FAIL.
acceptance_criteria: LUA-12 design decision: code-designer's first deliverable must declare whether ServiceCatalog becomes a field on ExecutionContext (the design §17.1 answer) or stays simulation-only (acceptable scope-out per the issue). The decision is irreversible for the lifetime of this run -- the same artifact drives the executor wiring and the test factory.

LUA-12 (decision = ExecutionContext owns ServiceCatalog path): add `service_catalog: *const ServiceCatalog` to ExecutionContext, modify call_service.zig's non-simulation branch to (a) call ctx.service_catalog.lookup(svc_id) and return a structured error table if missing, (b) build an HTTP request against service.endpoint_url respecting service.auth_method, (c) return a response table {status_code, headers, body} per design §17.1. Change return shape from `(string, number)` to single table. Tests per design §17.4 / tests/specs/LUA-12.md TC-LUA-12-01..15.

LUA-12 (decision = simulation-only path): explicitly mark LUA-12 as scope-deferred to a future WF-03 run; the only tests that pass are those that exercise the simulation path (already passing). Update docs/status/requirement_status.yaml to a new SCOPED status (or keep IN_PROGRESS with explicit 'simulation-only' annotation) and link the GH-592 decision comment.

LUA-15: move __failure_reason__ / __failure_details__ / __explicit_failure__ from _G to LUA_REGISTRYINDEX following the host_context.zig pattern (private keys, host_context.installContext analogues where appropriate). Read them back in executeSource's failed-pcall branch to set ScriptResult.error_kind = .ExplicitFailure when present, .RuntimeError otherwise. Tests per tests/specs/LUA-15.md TC-LUA-15-01..16, with explicit assertion that explicit failure is distinguishable from runtime error (TC-LUA-15-07).

LUA-16: implement captureStackTrace(L, allocator) using lua_getstack/lua_getinfo per design §21.2. After a failed pcall that is NOT an explicit failure (LUA-15's .RuntimeError branch), construct events.ScriptErrorPayload and surface it on ScriptResult -- but ONLY in a run that also lands LUA-08 (instruction_count source) and LUA-09 (memory_peak_bytes source). Tests per tests/specs/LUA-16.md TC-LUA-16-01..16. If LUA-08/09 are not landed in the same run, do NOT construct the ScriptErrorPayload at all -- a zero-valued instruction_count field in a payload is a worse test outcome than missing.

Sequencing note (already explicit in the issue): LUA-16 lands AFTER or alongside LUA-15 (shared executeSource branch and ScriptResult shape change) and AFTER LUA-08 (instruction_count field source). Fix sequencing for this run: LUA-15 first, then LUA-16 in the same run only if LUA-08 lands in the same run; otherwise LUA-16 must be deferred to a later run.
All three requirements restored to RELEASED with evidence, or the residual gap explicitly documented in CHANGELOG.md and on GH #592.
evidence_file: src/lua/host_api/call_service.zig lines 110-115 (the hardcoded '{}' non-simulation branch). src/lua/service_catalog.zig line 87 (`pub fn lookup(self, service_id) ?RegisteredService` -- the only definition in the entire source tree, zero call sites outside the definition itself; verified via workspace-wide grep_search for `ServiceCatalog` and `\.lookup(` on src/**/*.zig). src/lua/host_api/fail.zig lines 44/49/55 (three `lua_setglobal` writes) and the comment block at lines 11-18 naming the deferral; src/lua/host_context.zig lines 18-32 documenting the established registry-channel pattern that fail.zig was supposed to be migrated to. src/lua/events.zig lines 22-39 (ScriptErrorPayload, ScriptFailedPayload, Event, EventRecord) -- all defined, zero construction sites anywhere in src/lua/, verified via workspace grep. src/lua/instruction_limiter.zig lines 30-50 (installHook defined but commented as 'installed by no code path'). docs/design/lua-integration.md §17.1 (the design-intended implementation), §21.1-21.4 (the design-intended runtime error capture). docs/status/requirement_status.yaml (LUA-08/09/10/11/12/13/15/16 all IN_PROGRESS, MUST).
notes: This issue (ISS-0625) is batch 3 of the GH #495 / ISS-0169 LUA-08..16 verification tranche, scoped out by commit 33e3a25 because the 9-requirement parent scope was too large for one design/implementation pass. Sibling batch 2 (ISS-0624 / GH #591) covers LUA-11 (variable read/write) and LUA-13 (logging); sibling batch 1 (already landed, PR #505) covered LUA-05 (capability manifest) and LUA-06 (capability enforcement at call time) plus LUA-07 (manifest verification). Per the incidental-discovery protocol (CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only'), no NEW issue was discovered during diagnosis -- the three root causes above are all part of the GH-592 scope; nothing to forward to handoffs/global_queue.json.
resolution: Production code c5a12c9d, regression tests d0e74f73, integration tests 52c85455; CHANGELOG.md updated; requirements LUA-12/15/16 marked RELEASED; release decision at docs/status/release-WF03-GH592-2026-08-08.yaml
